verified: Read on 2026-09-25 from the full-text PDF of the article (the publisher page and the BNF site both returned HTTP 403, so the BNF could not be checked directly). mgPerKg and strengths: Table 1, Commonly used preparations of local anaesthetics: lidocaine 3 mg/kg at 1% and 2%; lidocaine with adrenaline 6 mg/kg at 1% and 2%; prilocaine 6 mg/kg and with adrenaline 8 mg/kg at 1% and 2%; bupivacaine 2 mg/kg and with adrenaline 2.5 mg/kg at 0.25% and 0.5%; ropivacaine 3 mg/kg and with adrenaline 4 mg/kg at 0.75% (the only ropivacaine strength in the table). Each row was checked against the table's dosage factor column (maximum dose divided by concentration, e.g. lidocaine 1% 0.3 mL/kg = 3 mg/kg). maxMg: the Discussion quotes the BNF 63rd edition maxima lidocaine 200 mg, bupivacaine 150 mg and prilocaine 400 mg and pairs them with 67, 75 and 67 kg, i.e. the plain mg/kg doses, so they are entered as plain-solution ceilings only. The source gives no mg ceiling for solutions with adrenaline or for ropivacaine, so those are null. Levobupivacaine is not in this source. Body weight rule and mixture rule in notes are from the section Instructions for use and the Discussion. Added 2026-09-25 from the other sources, each read on that date: levobupivacaine 2 mg/kg from the corrected Table 1 of Taylor and McLeod (BJA Education 2020; RCEMLearning also gives 2 mg/kg on lean body weight), with the 150 mg single-dose ceiling and 400 mg in 24 hours from the UK SmPC (levobupivacaine 2.5, 5 and 7.5 mg/ml are the injection strengths on emc; the SmPC gives no mg/kg dose and no preparation with adrenaline, so withAdrenaline is null); the 150 mg single-dose ceiling for bupivacaine with adrenaline from the UK SmPC of Bupivacaine and Adrenaline 0.5% (which gives no mg/kg dose), so it now matches the plain ceiling. Lidocaine with adrenaline stays at the source's 6 mg/kg: the UK SmPC gives only a 500 mg maximum single dose, and 7 mg/kg is in Taylor and McLeod Table 1 and the US Xylocaine label (dailymed.nlm.nih.gov, setid 27c2e78d-d037-470d-b4fa-44c33d78f788: 7 mg/kg, total not more than 500 mg); the note says so. The lipid emulsion note is the AAGBI 2010 regimen word for word in its numbers. ref on a drug or preparation names the source shown for it when it is not the first source.

notes: Use ideal (lean) body weight, not actual weight, in obesity, and use 70 kg for anyone weighing 70 kg or more: the source and the BNF base these doses on ideal body weight. This matters most where no mg ceiling is given (lidocaine or prilocaine with adrenaline, and ropivacaine). The mg ceiling applies whatever the weight.

Lidocaine with adrenaline: this tool uses the source's 6 mg/kg. Other references allow up to 7 mg/kg (BJA Education 2020, US product label), and the UK SmPC maximum single dose is 500 mg; at the 70 kg dosing cap the result here (420 mg) is within both.
Bupivacaine: the UK SmPC maximum single dose is 150 mg, plain or with adrenaline. Levobupivacaine: 2 mg/kg, not more than 150 mg as a single dose and 400 mg in 24 hours (UK SmPC).
Mixtures: calculate as if the whole volume were the agent with the greater toxic potential.
Toxicity varies with each patient's pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, so a dose within the maximum can still cause toxicity.

If toxicity is suspected, stop injecting, call for help and follow the local anaesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST) protocol. Lipid rescue (AAGBI 2010): 20% lipid emulsion 1.5 mL/kg IV over 1 min, then an infusion of 15 mL/kg/h (0.25 mL/kg/min). If the circulation is not restored or deteriorates, give up to 2 repeat boluses of 1.5 mL/kg 5 min apart and double the infusion to 30 mL/kg/h. Do not exceed a cumulative 12 mL/kg. In cardiac arrest, continue CPR throughout.
